note: Rewritten from Hill 1922, original in English (On some Australian termites of the genera Drepanotermes, Hamitermes and Leucotermes, Bulletin of Entomological Research 12, doi 10.1017/S0007485300045041). In 1915 the author had identified a dealate specimen as Termes rubriceps Froggatt (type locality McKinley Ranges, central Australia), and the present paper redescribes the alate and the soldier from specimens from Tennant's Creek and Leigh Creek in central Australia and Mullewa in Western Australia; the alates from Darwin (Northern Territory) were judged to belong to another new species, D. septentrionalis, the two being almost indistinguishable in soldier structure. The alate type series is in the South Australian Museum, the paratypes with the author. Hill uses the hyphen as a decimal point (e.g. 2-35 means 2.35 mm), and this entry changes it to a decimal point; the pronotum length and the hindwing width are damaged by OCR in the original (given as "|" and "9°25" respectively) and are not recorded; figs. 10—12 (alate head, wings, soldier head) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with D. silvestrii: the alate is larger, with longer and paler wings, a paler ventral abdomen, a much smaller fontanelle of different shape, larger compound eyes, fewer antennal segments (16 against 18) with distinctly different segmentation, and a much paler head and pronotum; the soldier is paler, with fewer wrinkles on the front of the head. Compared with the new species D. septentrionalis: the alate is larger, with longer and darker wings, a darker pronotum and 2 fewer antennal segments. Compared with D. perniger Frogg. (after Mjöberg's description): much larger, with much longer wings and different compound eyes, fontanelle and antennae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head very dark brown; clypeus yellow-ochre; antennae darker than the clypeus, brownish; mouthparts and venter antimony yellow; pronotum yellow-ochre with brown patches; wing pads and abdominal tergites dark brown (argus brown), the veins at the base of the wing pads dark; wings brown, the branches of the radius and cubitus very dark, the anterior margin pale. The head is large, rounded posteriorly, its upper surface flat, covered with numerous short fine pale hairs. The base of the labrum is narrow, the sides swollen, the anterior margin rounded. The anteclypeus is membranous, pointed in front. The postclypeus is of medium size, twice as wide as long, convex, its posterior margin rounded, its anterior margin truncate, the sides sloping. The fontanelle is very small, lanceolate, forked anteriorly. The compound eyes are large, moderately projecting, nearly circular (0.610 × 0.470 mm). The ocelli are large, oval, oblique, slightly less in length than the short diameter (horizontal diameter) of the compound eye, close to the compound eye, their anterior margin slightly behind the anterior margin of the compound eye. The mandibular dentition is as in D. silvestrii. The antennae are very long and slender, with 16 segments: segment 1 more than twice as long as segment 2; segment 3 about as long as segment 2, narrower and more spindle-shaped; segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 3 but wider, oval, always the shortest segment, though rarely markedly short; segment 5 longer and wider than segment 4; segment 6 slightly shorter and narrower than segment 5; segments 7—9 progressively longer; segments 10—14 about equal in length, slightly longer than segment 9; segments 15 and 16 slightly longer than segment 14 and equal to each other; segments 5—16 more or less stalked; segments 5—15 slightly spindle-shaped; segments 7—16 distinctly slender; the number and shape of the segments appear to be very stable. The pronotum is roughly triangular, setose and nearly flat, wider than long; the anterior margin slightly arched and turned up in the middle; the anterolateral corners rounded; the sides nearly straight, sloping steeply towards the rounded posterior margin; hairy. The mesonotum has a broad dark longitudinal band in the middle; the wing pads are large and setose, about two thirds of the length of the mesonotum. The metanotum is similar, but its wing pads are small, half of the visible part of the metanotum. The legs are as in D. silvestrii. The wings are very large and broad; the forewing slightly longer and slightly narrower than the hindwing; ciliate on the margins; the anterior margin distinctly yellow-ochre; the costa and the base of the radius dark, turning yellow posteriorly, the two veins distinctly separate over the proximal half of the wing and closer but still distinct over the distal half, meeting near the tip; the media is dark only at the base and elsewhere barely visible, running much closer to the cubitus; in the forewing the media separates from the radius within the wing pad, runs straight to the wing tip and gives off 5—6 indistinct upper branches; in the hindwing the media separates from the radius only after the wing suture and has 7—8 very faint branches, the proximal ones short and the others reaching the wing margin and entering it slightly above or below the tip; in the forewing the cubitus joins the posterior margin slightly below the wing tip and gives off 12—15 branches, of which the first 9—12 are very clear and some are forked; the hindwing generally has 12 branches, simple or forked once or twice; other variations are frequent. The abdomen is large; all the tergites bear short fine pale hairs, with a fringe of golden coarse hairs on the posterior margin; the sternites have indistinct brown spots at the sides; the cerci are very short and broad. Measurements (mm): length with wings 21—22; length without wings 11; head with mandibles length 2.35; head width (with compound eyes) 1.88; antennal length 3.29—3.75; right mandible length 0.94, width 0.75, left length 0.94, width 0.6; pronotum width 1.78 (its length is missing in the original); forewing length 18.3, width 5; hindwing length 17.5 (its width is missing in the original); tibiae (i) 1.36, (ii) 1.5, (iii) 2; abdominal width 3.5.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow-ochre to ochre-orange; labrum pale yellowish white; anterior margin of the clypeus with a transparent membranous edge; mandibles slightly darker than the head, darkest at the tip; the rest of the body pale yellow. The antennae are very long and slender, with 17 or 18 segments: segment 1 is long, more than twice as long as segment 2 and one third wider; segment 3 is as long as segment 2 but narrower; segment 4 is shorter than segment 3 but as wide, and more or less fused with segment 3; segment 5 is as long as segment 3 and narrow; segments 5—9 grow progressively longer, all slender and narrow; segments 10—18 are about equal in length, slightly shorter than segment 1. Measurements (mm): head with mandibles (crossed) length 2.82; head width 1.73; antennal length 3.57; thorax and abdomen length 3.29; pronotum length 0.6 and width 1.13; tibiae (i) 1.27, (ii) 1.45, (iii) 2.06.
